text:
Colton Parayko has no goals in 21 games, and Bleedin' Blue ran a piece listing three ways he's been one of the Blues' most disappointing players. That's a hard verdict on a player who was 30th among 215 defensemen in Evolving-Hockey's wins above replacement last season, with his defense at the 97th percentile.

Our numbers split the difference. St. Louis gets 48% of the expected goals with him on at five on five, a little worse than without him. He's at 20 minutes a night, still with elite tools: NHL Edge has his top speed at the 92nd percentile and his shot at the 89th. The goals will come (1.8 expected and nothing yet), and the Blues have scored 3.5 fewer than their chances deserve with him on.

He's 33, a Stanley Cup winner in 2019, and he played for Canada at the 2026 Olympics. The Blues have won five of their last six, so the team around him has found something.

What to watch: a first goal, and whether the defensive numbers return to last season's level as the minutes stabilize.
